problem.text: The change comments out two unused declarations: sampling's positive-infinity constant and the lane index inside fused RoPE normalization.

reasoning.text: These edits are consistent with suppressing unused-variable warnings without changing computation. Neither declaration supplies a precondition for the other edit.

impact.text: Sampling retains its negative-infinity masking, and RoPE retains its normalization arithmetic and launch geometry. No interface or dispatch changes occur.

source_notes.text: Read the initial sampling chapter and the fused-RoPE entry. They establish the existing native sampling implementation and the normalization kernel's previously recorded reduction and padded-read concerns.
The whole-parent search for 'compiler' also found compiler discovery in ext.py, a GEMM comment and calibration prose; those occurrences do not establish the warning diagnostics addressed here.

Issue #7, 'quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate', reports an extension-import failure; #29, 'Auto-YaRN for Qwen3? Maybe even set it dynamically?', discusses scaling policy. Their connection to this inspection is inferred from their references to util/rope.py, not evidence that this cleanup addresses either issue. Closed issue #16, 'RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument', concerns conversion failure attributed in its discussion to tokenizer truncation, not unused declarations.

limitations: No compiler invocation, CUDA test or warning log was available; warning removal and runtime equivalence were not measured.
The Python bounds calculation models integer launch arithmetic only, not emitted GPU loads, memory faults or scheduling.
Caller inspection establishes the native rope wrapper and RoPE.apply path, not exhaustive reach through dynamic or external consumers.

chapters.title: Remove unused declarations without changing kernels

claims.text: POS_INF_F32 has only its declaration in the parent-tree literal search. Commenting it out leaves NEG_INF_F32 active for masked logits and initial maxima; it does not change Gumbel noise or argmax selection.

RoPE's deleted lane expression computes threadIdx.x modulo 32, while the retained division by 32 identifies the warp. The lane value was never consumed. In particular, commenting it out does not add a lane-zero guard to the shared reduction store; the inherited normalization concern remains.

A scalar calculation of the unchanged launch formula gives 64 x-threads for an 80-element head: 24 frequency indices and 48 half-weight elements exceed their logical full-width arrays. The cleanup does not change these bounds.

findings.description: The fused normalization shared-store race is carried over, not repaired by removing the unused lane index.
findings.trigger: Enable fused normalization with nonuniform per-lane squared activation sums.
findings.expected_behavior: Store the complete warp reduction once, using a lane-zero guard as block_reduce_sum_f does.
findings.actual_behavior: Every lane writes its shuffle-down result to the same shared slot before normalization reads it. The native rope wrapper launches this kernel, and the inspected RoPE.apply call forwards optional normalization weights.

verification.description: Compared the unguarded store with the existing guarded reduction helper and traced the native wrapper and Python extension call.
verification.limits: No GPU race detection or observed numerical result.

findings.description: RoPE's unguarded frequency and normalization-weight reads remain unchanged.
findings.trigger: Use a head width not divisible by 64, or rotary frequencies shorter than the launched x dimension.
findings.expected_behavior: Padded lanes avoid reads beyond the logical frequency and normalization-weight arrays.
findings.actual_behavior: All x-threads read inv_freq[t]; normalization also reads a half2 weight without a head-width guard. RoPE.apply forwards the frequency and weight tensors without padding them in the inspected call path.

verification.description: Evaluated the inspected launch formula for head width 80, yielding 64 threads versus 40 frequency entries and 80 half-weight elements.
verification.limits: Integer bounds model only; no CUDA execution or demonstrated memory fault.

annotation.summary: Comments out two unused CUDA declarations to address compiler warnings; computation is unchanged, including inherited RoPE reduction and bounds concerns.
